title: Interfaces as Java's multiple-inheritance solution
answer: Java avoids multiple superclass inheritance because inheriting implementation and state from two class parents can create ambiguity about which parent member or initialization path should win. Interfaces provide multiple type inheritance without multiple class state. When interfaces supply conflicting default methods, Java requires explicit resolution. AeroTopo's `Units implements Left, Right` overrides `units()` and deliberately selects `Left.super.units()`, making the conflict visible and controlled.
